title: Automated Canary Quarantine and Guided Hotfix Flow for Cross-Deployment Model Regressions
creator: Priya Rao
description: Implement an automated quarantine and guided hotfix workflow that isolates failing canaries across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, minimizes blast radius, and provides a step-by-step remediation path for oncall and SRE engineers. The feature should integrate with existing routing/fallback policies, KV cache reconciliation, and customer communication templates.
acceptance_criteria: Canaries that exceed configured quality or SLO thresholds are automatically moved to a quarantined slice with no tenant traffic impact
Quarantine action creates an auditable incident record and triggers the guided hotfix UI in Redwood Console
Guided hotfix flow provides: suggested model pin, rollback vs patch decision matrix, KV cache invalidation checklist, and one-click traffic rejoin
Metrics and traces for quarantined canaries are surfaced in a dedicated dashboard and included in incident emails
System supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private control planes and respects customer isolation and KMS constraints
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Detection & Triage - Extend quality monitors to emit structured quarantine events when canary error-rate, hallucination signals, or regression evals cross thresholds
Phase 2: Quarantine Mechanics - Add slice-level routing rule to instantaneously divert traffic away from a canary slice and mark its model variant as quarantined in the catalog
Phase 3: Guided Hotfix UI - Build Console workflow showing suggested remediations (pin older variant, apply patch image, or scale down canary), with links to PR templates and rollback playbooks
Phase 4: KV Cache Reconciliation - Add a reconciliation job to detect stale KV cache keys across worker pools and surface required invalidation steps. Provide one-click cache flush where permitted
Phase 5: Cross-Env Validation - Smoke tests for Hosted/Dedicated/Private including VPC constraints, and an opt-in dry-run that simulates quarantine without customer-facing changes
Phase 6: Runbook & Communication - Wire automatic customer-facing templated messages and internal Slack incident snippets; ensure runbook links to postmortem checklist

decisions_and_tradeoffs: Automatic quarantine is conservative: only triggered when both signal tiers (runtime metric + eval mismatch) cross thresholds to avoid noisy quarantines
We chose slice-level routing instead of individual tenant kills to keep remediation coarse-grained and reversible across deployment types
For Private deployments we will not support automated one-click cache flushes; instead, UI will generate an operator script due to restricted network access
Rollback vs patch guidance will default to rollback for regressions with high customer impact; hotpatch recommended when model variance is low and fix is config-only
review_feedback: PM (Ava Martinez): Add explicit customer opt-out for automatic quarantines for Dedicated customers on reserved pools
Design (Sofia Alvarez): Simplify wording around 'quarantine' to 'isolate' in customer-facing copy; keep technical term internal
SRE (Daniel Kim): Add synthetic traffic rehydration step in runbook before rejoin to prevent cold-start regressions
Security (Maya Patel): For Private deployments require a signed operator action for any state-changing remediation
